newsitem.title: USA: Daschle says White House Mexico meeting positive.
newsitem.headline: Daschle says White House Mexico meeting positive.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle said a White House meeting Monday to discuss President Clinton' decision to certify Mexico as cooperating in the drug war was positive, but no final decision was made.

"I heard it was a good meeting at the White House," said Daschle, who talked to the president and said Clinton "indicated he thought the discussion would lead to more negotiations and discussions in the next couple of days."
A House committee voted last week to overturn Clinton's finding that Mexico is cooperating in the anti-drug war but to waive imposition of sanctions against the Mexican government.
Disapproval measures have also been introduced in the Senate. Daschle said he did not expect the Senate to take up the issue this week and hoped the House would also put off action.

Daschle also said allegations that China may have tried to improperly influence U.S. elections, as well as the flap over Mexico's role in the war against drugs could "impede" debates on trade issues with those nations, such as Most Favored Nation status for China.
But he said that "in the end I don't think it's going to affect us a great deal."
